# `pos-box picture` commands

## `pos-box picture get`

Download a picture currently shown by a POS group. Needs pos.sell; unrelated attachments are never available through this command.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | pos.sell |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/pos-box.picture.get` |
| External binary body | output |

### CLI

`bookflow pos-box picture get 01J00000000000000000000001 --out drinks.png --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pos-box picture get", "input": {"attachment": "01J00000000000000000000001"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "transport": {"output_file": "/permitted-directory/receipt.pdf"}}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attachment` | `ATTACHMENT` | string | yes | no | — | The attachment id of an item's picture or thumbnail, as `item show` or `item query` gives it.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--out PATH` | Required output path on the calling machine. Publish atomically after verified bytes and successful completion; never overwrite an existing entry. The parent directory must exist. JSON metadata stays on stdout. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### External binary body

The registry declares one `output` body separately from the JSON input and output models.

Python: pass a caller-owned binary sink as `output_stream=` to `client.run('pos-box picture get', input, ...)` or the named command method. Paths and stream objects are never command JSON fields. The return value is typed JSON metadata.

The output table below describes metadata returned by CLI/Python. HTTP returns raw bytes with download headers; `X-Bookflow-Output` carries this same complete typed metadata. A Python sink can contain partial bytes after an error; accept it only after the call succeeds.

See [binary transfers](../transfers.md) for executable file examples, HTTP encoding, limits, dry runs, and local completion verification.

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/pos-box.picture.get`

Send metadata in `X-Bookflow-Input`; this command does not use the ordinary JSON command route. Send an empty request body. ## `pos-box picture set`

Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP as a group picture. Item boxes share their inventory item picture. Needs pos.layout. Point of sale must be enabled. Every write checks the layout revision from pos-box list.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | pos.layout |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/pos-box.picture.set` |
| External binary body | input |

### CLI

`bookflow pos-box picture set 01JPOSBOXEXAMPLE00000000001 drinks.png --expected-version 6 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pos-box picture set", "input": {"pos_box": "01JPOSBOXEXAMPLE00000000001", "original_filename": "drinks.png", "expected_version": 6}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change", "transport": {"input_file": "/permitted-directory/receipt.pdf"}}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | Current layout revision from pos-box list, not a box or company-settings version; zero is the unsaved category seed.; minimum 0 |
| `pos_box` | `POS_BOX` | string | yes | no | — | Box ID from pos-box list.; minimum length 1 |
| `original_filename` | `--original-filename` | string | yes | no | — | Basename of the uploaded image.; minimum length 1; maximum length 255; Required in JSON/Python; CLI defaults to PATH basename |
| `media_type` | `--media-type` | string | no | no | "application/octet-stream" | The image bytes decide the stored type.; maximum length 127; CLI guesses MIME type from PATH unless explicitly supplied |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `PATH` | Required input file on the calling machine. Original filename defaults to its basename; media type defaults to the guessed MIME type, or application/octet-stream. Explicit metadata options override these defaults. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### External binary body

The registry declares one `input` body separately from the JSON input and output models.

Python: pass a caller-owned binary source as `input_stream=` to `client.run('pos-box picture set', input, ...)` or the named command method. Paths and stream objects are never command JSON fields. The return value is typed JSON metadata.

JSON requires `original_filename`; the CLI supplies its PATH basename when omitted. Python and HTTP default `media_type` to `application/octet-stream`. `--original-filename` and `--media-type` override CLI inference.

See [binary transfers](../transfers.md) for executable file examples, HTTP encoding, limits, dry runs, and local completion verification.


### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/pos-box.picture.set`

Send metadata in `X-Bookflow-Input`; this command does not use the ordinary JSON command route. Send one raw application/octet-stream request body, without multipart or base64 body encoding. The response is JSON metadata. Use `?dry_run=true` to hash and preview without persistent staging or writes.
